extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers, conference organizers (program chairs, area/meta-reviewers), and developers of tools for automating or assisting conference peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating NLP systems and procedures to assist with conference peer-review workflows, including submission screening, reviewer–paper matching, review writing, discussion moderation, and post-review analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of limitations and broader ethical impact sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should include compulsory discussions of limitations and broader ethical impact when required by the venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several AI conferences require such sections (e.g., ACL rolling review); simple NLP automation can detect the presence of these sections to enforce editorial requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist-section correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors indicate paper sections where certain issues are discussed (e.g., reproducibility efforts, compensation to human participants, adherence to data licenses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated checks should verify that checklist answers correspond to the indicated paper sections to help authors avoid accidental errors, speed up checklist completion, and facilitate reviewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism and self-plagiarism screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Screen submissions for plagiarism and self-plagiarism as part of the initial screening stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detection is a core editorial/publishing rule; NLP tools can assist but may need to integrate with existing plagiarism-detection systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity-violation detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect violations of anonymity (e.g., explicit identity disclosures like 'as shown in our prior work').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated detection of identity-revealing content can help enforce double-blind or anonymized reviewing policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submission and duplicate submission detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect submissions concurrently submitted to different venues (dual submission) or duplicate submissions to the same venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screening should flag such policy violations to program chairs for action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection of fake paper mills
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect papers that appear to be produced by fake paper mills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use metadata and content signals (and potentially external reporting) to identify suspect submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection of machine-generated text and AI-use compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect potentially machine-generated text and enforce compliance with editorial guidelines on the use of AI for writing assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screening should check adherence to venue policies about AI-assisted writing and flag suspiciously generated content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial manuscript quality assessment (coherence, citation coverage, readability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess manuscript quality attributes such as coherence, citation coverage, and readability during screening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such analysis can help identify submissions for desk rejection or mentoring, balance reviewing load, and study effects of manuscript quality downstream.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text-similarity-based reviewer–paper scoring (with caveats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute similarity between submission text and reviewer publication history to score reviewer suitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware publication history may not reflect current interests; similarity can capture irrelevant criteria (notation, stylistic elements); dense representations often lack interpretability. These limitations reduce trust in similarity as sole assignment criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword-based reviewer–paper scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Score matches using manually provided keywords chosen from a pre-defined list (area, contribution type, language).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keywords are more interpretable and can explain matches, but poor keyword selection fails to differentiate many submissions. Assistance could include preparing effective keyword lists, suggesting keywords, imputing fractional scores for related keywords, and allowing free-form semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding as indicator of reviewer interest (not expertise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use reviewer bids to indicate interest/expertise for particular submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bids reflect interest (and strategic motives) rather than guaranteed expertise; bidding scales poorly with many papers. Combine bidding with similarity/keyword methods, limit which papers are offered for bidding, and consider bid counts to ensure adequate bids per paper. Beware strategic behavior and collusion facilitated by bidding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation of collusive or strategic bidding
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect and mitigate strategic bidding behaviors (favoring friends/competitors, forming collusion rings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigations include constraining bidding formats (e.g., require a minimum number of positive bids), constraining matching, combining bid data with NLP analysis of review texts and metadata, and exploring algorithms beyond bidding data alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of matching signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine multiple signals (text similarity, keywords, bidding) into a single aggregate reviewer–paper score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conferences use heuristics or fixed formulas; choice of aggregation is nontrivial. Principled approaches include post-hoc evaluation of counterfactual methods and merging NLP-based review evaluations with causal inference to choose assignment methods more rigorously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-interest (COI) identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify conflicts prohibiting assignment of a reviewer to a paper (co-authorship, supervisory relationships, shared grants, same institution, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic inference via DBLP/Semantic Scholar/ORCID profiles helps but is challenged by incomplete sources and name-disambiguation; more advanced NLP is needed to infer supervisory or other non-coauthorship conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name disambiguation and external-data mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Robustly map individuals across external databases despite name variations and changing affiliations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential for reliable COI inference and correct attribution; requires NLP and integration with web services/databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reducing incentives for strategic matches in optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust matching constraints/objective to reduce effectiveness of collusion and reciprocity-based strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: penalize matches with multiple reviewers from the same geographic area, penalize reviewer pairs that coauthored, penalize '2-cycles' where reviewers bid on each other's papers, and add randomness to matching scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritizing and curating good reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Use past-reviewer performance data (on-time submission, review length, participation in rebuttal/discussion) to give well-performing reviewers priority in assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While useful, using past data raises privacy/de-anonymization risks; consider privacy-preserving techniques (anonymization, differential privacy). NLP-based assessment of past review quality can augment metadata-based metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual assignment support to identify missing expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Assist human PC/meta-reviewers by identifying required expertise not present among assigned reviewers, especially for emerging or interdisciplinary submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NLP tools can detect 'rare' topics or languages, suggest appropriate reviewers, explain why particular expertise is needed, and facilitate invitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Augmented reading (reviewer reading assistance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide AI-powered reading interfaces that highlight manuscript aspects (contributions, experimental setup, findings) and assist navigation (symbol definitions, Q&A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guided reviewing interfaces can especially help novice reviewers; frameworks exist for developing such tools (SCIM, ScholarPhi, ReviewFlow).

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature assistance during review
rubrics_metrics.description: Help reviewers find relevant prior work, detect missing citations, and assess whether referenced works are cited appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citation recommendation and fact-checking tools can guide novelty judgments and help avoid unjustified 'lack-of-novelty' criticisms. Custom search engines can hide public versions of the manuscript to avoid de-anonymization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection of manuscript technical flaws
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify mathematical mistakes, conceptual fallacies, and problems in experimental design and methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generative AI and multimodal NLP could detect errors and check correspondence between figures/tables and text; tools can nudge reviewers to typical pitfalls and verify compliance with domain experimental standards (computational costs, statistical testing, participant details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone, clarity, and substantiation in review text
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should be polite, specific, and substantiated; avoid rudeness, vagueness, and unsupported claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use politeness analysis, specificity analysis, hedging detection, and matching reviewer comments to manuscript content to find unanchored or misaligned claims; flag inconsistency between reviewer claims and paper content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection of heuristics and strategic behavior in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect heuristic-based or strategically-motivated review arguments (e.g., 'results are not surprising', enforced self-citations, 'torpedo reviews').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish heuristics from legitimate critique: flag heuristics only when claims are unsubstantiated or contradicted by evidence. Combine surface-level analysis with checks against content and related work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection of plagiarized or fake reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify reviews that appear plagiarized or generated by malicious/fake sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NLP tools can help detect such anomalous reviews for further investigation (Piniewski et al., 2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and pragmatic structure of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure reviews follow community-accepted composition standards (argument roles like strength, weakness, todo, summary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourse/pragmatic tagging and argument-mining can label sentences and discover argumentative structure. Structured and semi-structured review forms improve inter-rater agreement; NLP can pre-fill forms, detect inconsistencies (e.g., substantial weakness listed as a question), and use structured data as weak supervision for essay-style review analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring schema and calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: Use overall scores, confidence scores, and optional criteria scores (novelty, soundness, impact, excitement); address calibration and commensuration biases across reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calibration issues arise from differing score interpretations and from combining criteria differently. NLP-based score prediction can detect inconsistencies between review text and numeric scores, identify over/under-confident reviews, and extract reviewer preferences to mitigate commensuration bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-response composition and rebuttal support
rubrics_metrics.description: Assist authors in writing productive, well-structured, and appropriately toned rebuttals that address reviewer concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use argument mining, pragmatic tagging, politeness and specificity analysis; extract key action items/questions from reviews and aggregate concerns to help plan responses. Rebuttal generation work exists (attitude- and theme-guided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualizing and monitoring post-review discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Map parts of the discussion to the relevant manuscript passages, connect author responses to specific reviews, and highlight responses that address criticisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-document analysis can give reviewers pointers to manuscript parts under discussion; tools can report changes in submission text in response to reviews and map response text to review items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized notifications and mandatory-intervention alerts
rubrics_metrics.description: Notify participants of discussion updates relevant to them and alert meta-reviewers when their intervention is mandatory (e.g., open conflicts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NLP can detect which updates concern each participant to avoid overwhelming or insufficient notifications; systems should support different CMS notification affordances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking anchoring and herding effects in discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Detect and flag undue influence among reviewers (anchoring/herding) during discussion that could bias final judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze the discussion and subsequent review changes to track influence patterns and flag reviewers unduly influencing others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increasing participation through personalized nudges
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase reviewer engagement in discussion via personalized reminders and nudges rather than generic, often-ignored reminders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NLP can pre-fill personalized reminder templates, generate emails for meta-reviewer approval, detect unanswered or insufficiently-followed reviewer statements (e.g., author addressed concern but reviewer didn't update score), and surface such cases early for meta-reviewer action.
